audience_profile: Senior engineers who use CDNs but may not have looked at CloudFront's scale, Netflix's in-ISP appliances, or a real X-Cache/Age response.
learning_objective: Explain why a stream starts fast: copies near viewers (CloudFront POPs, Netflix Open Connect inside ISPs), what a miss and a hit do, and how to see it in real headers.
creative_concept: Start on the real night Earth over London, show the cost of one distant origin, light up the edge network, step inside an ISP, then prove miss and hit with a real response.

treatments.name: A. Real Earth to real headers
treatments.shape: globe hook, globe problem, counter, globe network, 3D appliance, ISP path, split-screen miss/hit, sequence, real terminal, stacking benefits
treatments.verdict: Chosen: concrete geography, sourced scale, and a proof the viewer can reproduce.

treatments.name: B. Diagram-only walkthrough
treatments.shape: iconflow and sequence for every step
treatments.verdict: Rejected: precise but static for 60 s on a phone.

treatments.name: C. Numbers-led explainer
treatments.shape: charts of latency and hit ratio
treatments.verdict: Rejected: needs figures no official page gives.

chosen: A. Real Earth to real headers
hook: Night Earth, the camera flies into London: Netflix in London: instant. Why?
narrative_structure: Question; one distant origin; the CDN idea with a sourced count; the edge network lights up; Netflix Open Connect; inside the ISP; miss versus hit; steps on a miss; real response; benefits and the answer.
visual_direction: noir-network, real NASA night imagery for the globe scenes, glowing city points, arcs with light-trail packets, no decorative shapes.
narration_approach: Short sentences, real names (CloudFront, Open Connect, X-Cache, Age), us-east-1 spoken as U S East 1.
